correctness.rationale: The ruler representation Z_n[p]=a_(1+ν2(p)) reduces nonsingleton Lyndon factors to odd-to-even aligned substrings. Every other starting or ending parity supplies an immediately smaller proper suffix. The doubled length-two code phi(a_j)=a1 a_j reflects lexicographic comparisons and preserves Lyndon status for lower-rank factors, giving an induction and explicit base case. Each occurrence of a_j is preceded by the exact Z_(j-1) central context, proving j endpoint suffixes; summing endpoint counts gives n(n+1)/2 distinct, 2^(n−i+1)−1 occurrences at each length 2^(i-1), total 2^(n+1)−n−2. The decreasing half-Zimin prefix factorization gives CFL. Independent direct suffix comparison at every endpoint ranks 1..7 exactly matched the theorem; this is a check, not all-n induction.

value.rationale: The exponentially long canonical Zimin words are standard unavoidable-pattern objects; an O(n²)-size full Lyndon-factor specification plus pointwise ending-suffix profiles, exact lacunary lengths and multiplicities is a motivated complete classification of a natural string combinatorics invariant.

final_claim: For every n>=1 with ordered distinct letters a1<...<an, all Lyndon factors of the finite Zimin word Z_n are exactly {Z_(i-1)a_j:1<=i<=j<=n}; at each position p with j=1+v2(p), precisely j Lyndon factors end, with lengths 1,2,4,...,2^(j-1). This yields distinct and occurrence spectra and the canonical Chen–Fox–Lyndon factorization.
limitations: Alphabet strictly ordered and rank dependent; literal finite words, not re-ordered alphabets or pattern morphisms.
Independent brute-force check n<=7; induction handles all n.
